# Jubilees Chapter 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abraham Blesses Jacob and Dies

---

**22:1** In the first year of the first week of the forty-third jubilee, Abraham came back and settled at Mamre, opposite Hebron.

**22:2** Isaac slaughtered a peace offering and brought it to his father, and they all sat and ate together — Abraham, Isaac, Isaac's wife, Ishmael's wife, everyone. Abraham's heart was full of joy because of Isaac's offering.

**22:3** During those days, Isaac also offered a peace offering to the LORD. At the Feast of First-Fruits, he sent his father Abraham some of the first produce from his fields — firstfruits and firstborn animals.

**22:4** Abraham was overwhelmed with joy and praised the Most High God who made heaven and earth, who filled the earth with good things and gave them to humanity so that people could eat and drink and give thanks to their Creator.

**22:5** "Thank you, my God, for letting me see this day. I am one hundred and seventy-five years old — I have lived a full life, and all my days have been filled with peace."

**22:6** "I kept myself separate from the nations and their pollution. I lived among them, but I never followed their ways or their disgusting practices."

**22:7** "You are the living God, and you know what was in my heart — I wanted to do your will, to walk a straight path. I never swerved from it, not once in all my life."

**22:8** Then Abraham called out, "Jacob! Come here, my son — let me hold you. Come close so I can kiss you, my dear child."

**22:9** Jacob came close, and Abraham kissed him and said, "My son, my joy — nothing on this earth makes me happier than you do. May the LORD bless you always. May you be blessed above everyone alive, because you are the light and the lord of the nations, the son of Abraham — and Abraham was counted righteous before God."

**22:10** "In you and your descendants, the joy of Abraham will live on before the LORD. You will be honored as a prince and blessed forever. So now I charge you, my son: live by Abraham's way. Keep his righteousness. Walk his path."

**22:11** "Don't mix with the nations. Don't sit at their tables. Don't copy their lives or make yourself their close companion — their practices are impure, and everything they do is offensive to God."

**22:12** "They make sacrifices to dead things and bow down to demons. They hold feasts at gravesites. Everything they do is empty and worthless."

**22:13** "They don't think clearly — their eyes can't see how ridiculous they are when they say to a piece of wood, 'You're my god,' or to a rock, 'You're my lord, my rescuer.' Wood and stone have no hearts, and neither do they."

**22:14** "Jacob, my son — may God Most High help you. May the God of heaven bless you and keep you far away from their impurity and their confusion."

**22:15** "Be very careful, Jacob: do not marry any woman from Canaan's line. The whole Canaanite people is going to be rooted out of this land. Ham sinned, and Canaan sinned with him — their whole line is marked for destruction and exile. Whatever survives will be scattered across the earth."

**22:16** "That's why Noah cursed Canaan — because of Ham's sin. Canaan's people will be uprooted entirely because of the corrupt things they did."

**22:17** "So now, my son — here are all my instructions. Keep them. Don't take a Canaanite wife. Find a woman from my own family line — a wife who is worthy of you."

**22:18** "May the LORD God of Abraham bless you and your children, and make you a holy nation, shaped by his own will, keeping his law and his ways. May he be your Father, and may you be his firstborn son and people — now and forever."

**22:19** "Go in peace, my son. May the Most High — my God, your God — give you strength to do his will and bless all your children and all the remnant of my line, through every generation, forever, with the same blessing he gave to me."

**22:20** Abraham finished blessing Jacob. Then he lay down on his bed — and he was gathered to his ancestors.

**22:21** After Abraham died, Jacob stayed close to his father Isaac. Isaac loved Jacob deeply.

**22:22** In those days, Isaac and Ishmael had come from Beersheba to be with Abraham during the feast days. Ishmael brought his sons — four of his older sons and six younger ones who were still alive — and they all gathered together.

**22:23** The servants of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Ishmael all came together and buried Abraham — in the cave at Machpelah, beside Sarah his wife, in the field Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite, facing Mamre.

**22:24** They mourned for Abraham for forty days — all his household, Isaac, Ishmael, all their children, all of Keturah's sons in their own places. The grief was immense.

---
*PNEUMA notes: This chapter is emotionally rich — Abraham's thanksgiving prayer, his deathbed blessing of Jacob, and the family gathering. The blessing of Jacob here is unique to Jubilees and serves as a direct patriarchal transmission bypassing Isaac (who will give his own blessing in Gen 27/Jub 26). "First-Fruits" festival = Shavuot, Jubilees' central covenant occasion.*
